newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares surge after coalition seeks polls.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares surge after coalition seeks polls.

text.p: Turkish shares jumped nearly four percent on Monday in the wake of the Islamist-led government's call for early elections, shrugging off concern about further political uncertainty, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 index .XU100 ended the day up 3.76 percent, or 60 points, at 1,655, off an intraday high of 1,673. It rose 8.7 percent last week mainly on hopes of an alternative alliance to replace the crumbling coalition under Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
The prospect of a fresh government alliance outweighed the potentially unsettling impact of elections. brokers said. The trading sector posted the strongest gains, rising nearly 13 percent.
"I think the market is still buying on expectations of an alternative government because there is no other solid development to boost the shares," said Tolga Ozkan Okay from Evis Securities.

Trading volume eased to 31.97 trillion lira ($225.6 million) from Friday's 32.69 trillion. Nearly a quarter of trading was in utilities Cukurova Elektrik and Aktas Elektrik and national carrier Turkish Airlines.

The government's conservative coalition partners said on Monday early elections would be held this year under a deal between Erbakan and his deputy Tansu Ciller to ease pressure from the generals to carry out an anti-Islamist crackdown.

Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, announced on Sunday he would step down in favour of True Path leader Ciller within a month. He said Foreign Minister Ciller would then head a caretaker government to go to elections, but set no date.
"The market does not believe that parliament approval for early polls this year can be secured because the legal procedures cannot be completed in time," said Hasan Soydan from Garanti Securities.
The distant prospect of elections did not trouble sentiment, brokers said.
"Elections seem far away when considering the average maturity for our (stock) investors is 15 days," said Erhan Topac, general manger of Gedik Securities.

Some brokers said the possibility of a caretaker leader from outside the existing alliance, such as main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz of the conservative Motherland Party, supported the strong early rally.
A benign technical scenario reinforced the uptrend, which came on the heels of a 4.3 percent gain on Friday and was further boosted by a break through resistance at 1,600 points.
But brokers said there was strong resistance above 1,700, the index's all-time high close on January 27.
"There is resistance at 1,750 points. The volume of trading is good and it could continue to this level. But at that point selling could emerge," said Seyfullah Esen of Gedik Securities.

Expectation of a Treasury auction supported the bond market, where yields fell by around half a percentage point to around 102 percent despite tight liquidity which pushed up overnight money and repo rates slightly.
Bankers expect low demand and higher risk premium and low demand in Tuesday's two-year, inflation-indexed bond auction due to mounting political uncertainty.
The treasury had sold 55.27 trillion lira of two-year bonds at 29.95 percent risk premium at its last auction on May 13, up from a 25 percent risk premium in the previous auction.
In the currency market, the strong demand for dollars seen last week faded. The Turkish lira fell to 141,720 against the dollar from 140,410 at Friday's close.
